mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates one signed difference to another, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D). Without this, the model may treat the equality as an absolute difference or swap the terms, leading to incorrect equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement says 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of Y that C has and D'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has more than Y' in a signed difference equality as |X - Y| = ... or swapping X and Y, producing the wrong relationship.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number, but keep it mutable for later transfers. Without this, the model may treat the count as immutable and miss updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the text says 'Person has N items'.
mathgap.example: Assigning a person's count from a direct statement and then never updating it despite later transfers that change that count.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has N more items than Y' as X = Y + N, and 'X has N fewer items than Y' as X = Y - N. Without this, the model may reverse the sign and produce wrong counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the phrases 'more than' or 'fewer than'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has N fewer items than Y' as X = Y + N instead of X = Y - N.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, assign each recipient half of the giver's current count and set the giver's count to zero. Without this, the model may give each recipient the full amount or forget to zero the giver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the text mentions a person splitting all of their items equally between two others.
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient the full original amount instead of half, and not reducing the giver's count to zero.

mathgap.title: Targeted constraint extraction for queried variable
mathgap.principle: When the goal is to find a specific person's count, first gather all equations and statements that involve that person throughout the entire problem. Without this, the model may miss later constraints that affect the queried variable.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, after identifying the queried person, scan the whole problem for any mention of that person.
mathgap.example: Only using early equations about Hakeem and ignoring later transfers or difference statements that also involve Hakeem.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, updating their current counts. Without this, the model may forget to adjust one side of the transfer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the text says 'A gives X items to B'.
mathgap.example: Processing a transfer but forgetting to subtract X from A or add X to B, leaving counts inconsistent.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known from a direct statement or previous deduction, substitute its numeric value before solving the equality. Without this, the model may leave the equation unsimplified and miss the numeric relationship.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a signed difference equality contains a term that has been previously determined (e.g., Icie = Evie + 9).
mathgap.example: Having Evie - Icie = Hakeem - Moises but not substituting Icie = Evie + 9, leaving the left side unevaluated.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given, updating counts after each step; later statements refer to the updated counts. Without this, the model may treat all constraints as simultaneous and ignore the effect of earlier transfers on later equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Throughout the solution, read the problem line by line and apply each operation before moving to the next.
mathgap.example: Solving all equations as if they were simultaneous, ignoring that a later transfer changes a person's count used in an earlier‑appearing equality.

mathgap.title: Preserve order in signed difference statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions the 'difference between X and Y', treat it as the signed difference X - Y, not the absolute value or Y - X. Without this, the model may invert the sign and obtain the wrong relationship.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase like 'the difference between X and Y' appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between X and Y' as |X - Y| or swapping to Y - X, leading to an incorrect equation.

mathgap.title: Deferred absolute resolution of signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: When a signed difference equality is encountered, express the relationship but do not assign final absolute values to the involved variables if they later appear in transfer statements; instead, apply subsequent transfers to those variables before solving for the queried variable. Without this, the model may compute a provisional answer and ignore later changes, yielding an incorrect final count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a signed difference equality involves variables that are later referenced in transfer statements or additional constraints.
mathgap.example: Using Evie - Icie = Hakeem - Moises to compute Hakeem's count, then stopping without applying later transfers that give Hakeem additional potatoes.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses signed differences with absolute differences and forgets the importance of the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order X - Y as stated; treat the difference as signed, not absolute, and never swap the terms unless the text explicitly does so.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes transfers are commutative and processes them out of order or all at once.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer in the exact order it appears, updating the giver's and receiver's counts immediately.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a direct count as a fixed final value, overlooking later transfers that modify that count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as initial values; apply any subsequent transfers to adjust them.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model overlooks clauses that restrict when a transfer occurs, treating every transfer as unconditional.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Parse the full statement, including any conditions, and apply the transfer only if the condition holds.

mathgap.description: Premature termination before processing all statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model stops once it finds a relationship that seems to determine the queried variable, assuming no further information will affect it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: After solving any sub‑equation, continue scanning the entire problem for any additional statements involving the queried variable, especially later transfers or constraints, and incorporate them before finalizing the answer.
